edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), De idololatria, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Sed luceant, inquit, opera vestra. At nunc lucent tabernae et januae nostrae: plures jam invenies ethnicorum fores sine lucernis et laureis quam Christianorum. De ista quoque specie quid videtur? Si idoli honor est, sine dubio idoli honor idololatria est. Si hominis caussa est, recogitemus omnem idololatriam in hominis caussam esse. Recogitemus omnem idololatriam in homines esse culturam, cum ipsos deos nationum homines retro fuisse, etiam apud suos constet. Itaque nihil interest, superioris, an hujus saeculi viris superstitio ista praestetur. Idololatria non propter personas quae opponuntur, sed propter officia ista damnata est, quae ad daemones pertinent. Reddenda sunt Caesari quae sunt Caesaris, bene quod opposuit, et quae sunt Dei Deo. Quae ergo sunt Caesaris? scilicet de quibus tunc consultatio movebatur, praestandusne esset census Caesari, an non. Ideo et monetam ostendi sibi Dominus postulavit, et de imagine, cujus esset, requisivit. Et cum audisset, Caesaris: Reddite, ait, quae sunt Caesaris Caesari, et quae sunt Dei Deo; id est imaginem Caesaris Caesari, quae in nummo est, et imaginem Dei Deo, quae in homine est: ut Caesari quidem pecuniam reddas, Deo temetipsum. Alioquin, quid erit Dei, si omnia Caesaris? Ergo, inquis, honor Dei est, lucernae pro foribus, et laurus in postibus? non utique quod Dei honor est, sed quod ejus qui pro Deo hujusmodi officiis honoratur, quantum in manifesto est, salva operatione quae est in occulto, ad daemonia perveniens. Certi enim esse debemus, si quos latet per ignorantiam litteraturae saecularis, etiam ostiorum deos apud Romanos, Cardeam a cardinibus appellatam, et Forculum a foribus, et Limentinum a limine, et ipsum Janum a janua: et utique scimus, licet nomina inania atque conficta sint, cum tamen in superstitionem deducuntur, rapere ad se daemonia et omnem spiritum immundum per consecrationis obligamentum. Alioquin daemonia nullum habent nomen singulatim, sed ibi nomen inveniunt, ubi et pignus. Etiam apud Graecos Apollinem θυραῖον, et Antelios daemonas ostiorum praesides legimus. Haec igitur ab initio praevidens Spiritus sanctus, etiam ostia in superstitionem ventura praececinit per antiquissimum prophetam Enoch. Nam et alia ostia in balneis adorari videmus. Si autem eorum sunt quae in ostiis adorentur, ad eos et lucernae et laureae pertinebunt. Idolo feceris, quicquid ostio feceris. Hoc in loco ex auctoritate quoque Dei contestor, quia nec tutum est subtrahere quodcumque uni fuerit ostensum, utique omnium caussa. Scio fratrem per visionem eadem nocte castigatum graviter, quod januam ejus subito annuntiatis gaudiis publicis servi coronassent. Et tamen non ipse coronaverat, aut praeceperat, nam ante processerat, et regressus reprehenderat factum: adeo apud Dominum in hujusmodi etiam disciplina familiae nostrae aestimatur. Igitur quod attineat ad honores regum vel imperatorum, satis praescriptum habemus, in omni obsequio esse nos oportere, secundum Apostoli praeceptum, subditos magistratibus et principibus et potestatibus: sed intra limites disciplinae, quousque ab idololatria separamur. Propterea enim et illud exemplum trium fratrum praecucurrit, qui alias obsequentes erga regem Nabuchodonosor, honorem imaginis ejus constantissime respuerunt, probantes idololatriam esse, quicquid ultra humani honoris modum ad instar divinae sublimitatis extollitur. Sic et Daniel caetera Dario subnixus, tamdiu fuit in officio, quamdiu a periculo disciplinae vacaret. Nam id ne subiret, non magis leones regios timuit, quam illi regios ignes. Accendant igitur quotidie lucernas, quibus lux nulla est, affigant postibus lauros postmodum arsuras, quibus ignes imminent; illis competunt et testimonia tenebrarum, et auspicia poenarum. Tu lumen es mundi, et arbor virens semper. Si templis renuntiasti, ne feceris templum januam tuam. Minus dixi: si lupanaribus renuntiasti, ne indueris domi tuae faciem novi lupanaris.
pass_a_gloss: But let, he says, your works shine. But now our shops and doorways shine: you will find more doorways of pagans without lamps and laurels than of Christians. What seems to be the case with this kind of thing? If it is honor to idols, without doubt idol honor is idolatry. If it is for the sake of man, let us consider that all idolatry is for the sake of man. Let us consider that all idolatry is worship of men, since even the gods of the nations were once men, as is also agreed among their own people. Therefore, it makes no difference whether this superstition is offered to the men of a former age or of this age. Idolatry is condemned not because of the persons to whom it is offered, but because of these offices which pertain to demons. Let us render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. What, then, are Caesar's? Certainly those things about which the consultation was then being held, whether the census should be paid to Caesar or not. For this reason, the Lord also showed them a coin and asked whose image was on it. And when they heard, 'Caesar's', he said, 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's'; that is, render to Caesar the image of Caesar, which is on the coin, and to God the image of God, which is in man: so that to Caesar you should render money, but to God yourself. Otherwise, what will be God's if all things are Caesar's? Therefore, you say, is the honor of God lamps before doorways and laurels on doorposts? Not at all, because the honor of God is not this, but because the one who is honored by such offices on behalf of God, as far as what is manifest is concerned, saving the operation which is in secret, reaches to demons. For we ought to be certain, if it is hidden from some through ignorance of secular literature, that even the gods of doorways among the Romans, Cardea called from hinges, and Forculus from doors, and Limentinus from thresholds, and Janus himself from doorways: and certainly we know, although the names are empty and fabricated, that when they are led into superstition, they snatch demons and every unclean spirit through the obligation of consecration. Otherwise, demons have no name individually, but they find a name where they also find a pledge. We also read among the Greeks that Apollo is called θυραῖον, and Antelios, demons who preside over doorways. The Holy Spirit, therefore, foreseeing these things from the beginning, also prophesied about doorways coming into superstition through the most ancient prophet Enoch. For we see that other doorways in baths are also worshiped. But if the things that are worshiped on doorways belong to them, then lamps and laurels will also pertain to them. You do to an idol whatever you do to a doorway. I testify to this in this place also by the authority of God, because it is not safe to withhold whatever has been shown to anyone, certainly for the sake of all. I know a brother who was severely rebuked through a vision on the same night, because his servants had suddenly crowned his doorway with garlands on the announcement of public joys. And yet he himself had not crowned it, nor had he ordered it, for he had gone out beforehand and had returned to rebuke the deed: so much is our family's discipline esteemed by the Lord in such matters. Therefore, as far as the honors of kings or emperors are concerned, we have a sufficient prescription, that we ought to be obedient in all service, according to the apostle's precept, subject to magistrates and princes and powers: but within the limits of discipline, as far as we are separated from idolatry. For this reason, the example of the three brothers also comes first, who, although otherwise obedient to King Nebuchadnezzar, constantly refused the honor of his image, proving that idolatry is whatever is extolled beyond the measure of human honor to the likeness of divine sublimity. So also Daniel, supporting Darius in other things, was in office as long as he was free from the danger of discipline. For he did not undergo this, no more than he feared the royal lions, than those royal fires. Let them light lamps every day, therefore, to which no light is given, let them affix laurels to doorposts which will soon wither, to which fires are imminent; these are fitting for them, both the testimonies of darkness and the auspices of punishments. You are the light of the world, and a always green tree. If you have renounced temples, do not make your doorway a temple. I have said less: if you have renounced brothels, do not assume the face of a new brothel in your own home.

pass_b_english: But let your works shine, he says. Yet now our shops and doorways are the ones blazing with light; you will find more pagan thresholds bare of lamps and laurels than Christian ones. What is really going on here? If this is honor paid to idols, then beyond doubt it is idolatry. If it is done for humanity's sake, consider that all idolatry is ultimately practiced for humanity's sake. Consider that all idolatry is the worship of men, since even the nations' gods were once human beings, as their own traditions confirm. So it makes no difference whether this superstition is offered to the men of a former age or to the men of this one. Idolatry stands condemned not because of the persons to whom it is directed, but because of the rites themselves, which belong to demons. "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matt 22:21). What then belongs to Caesar? Precisely the matters under debate at that time — whether the census tax should be paid to Caesar or not. That is why the Lord asked to see a coin and questioned whose image it bore. When they answered, "Caesar's," he replied, "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matt 22:21); that is, hand over to Caesar the image of Caesar stamped on the coin, and to God the image of God stamped on humanity — so that you give Caesar money, but give God yourself. Otherwise, what will belong to God if everything belongs to Caesar? So you claim, then, that lamps at doorways and laurels on doorposts are honor to God? Not at all; it is not because this honors God, but because the one who is honored by such rites on God's behalf — as far as outward appearances go, while the hidden operation reaches demons — is being worshiped. We must be certain of this: even if some are ignorant of secular literature, the Romans have gods of doorways — Cardea named from hinges, Forculus from doors, Limentinus from thresholds, and Janus himself from doorways. And we know for a fact that, although these names are empty fabrications, once they are drawn into superstition they seize demons and every unclean spirit through the bond of consecration. Otherwise demons have no individual names, but they find a name wherever they find a pledge. Among the Greeks we also read of Apollo called Thyraios, and the Antelii, demons who preside over doorways. The Holy Spirit, foreseeing these things from the beginning, prophesied through the most ancient prophet Enoch that even doorways would fall into superstition. We see, too, that other doorways in bathhouses are worshiped. But if the beings worshiped at doorways belong to them, then lamps and laurels pertain to them as well. Whatever you do to a doorway, you do to an idol. I testify to this here by the very authority of God, because it is not safe to withhold what has been shown to anyone, especially for the sake of all. I know a brother who was severely rebuked in a vision that very night because his servants had suddenly garlanded his doorway when public rejoicing was announced. He himself had not garlanded it, nor ordered it; he had gone out beforehand and returned to rebuke the act — so highly does the Lord esteem our household discipline in such matters. Therefore, concerning honors paid to kings or emperors, we have a clear rule: we must render full obedience, according to the apostle's precept, subject to magistrates, princes, and powers — but within the limits of our discipline, as long as we are kept separate from idolatry. For this reason the example of the three brothers comes first: though otherwise obedient to King Nebuchadnezzar, they steadfastly refused to honor his image, proving that idolatry is whatever is exalted beyond the measure of human honor to the likeness of divine sublimity (Dan 3:18). So also Daniel, while supporting Darius in other matters, remained in office only as long as he was free from the danger of compromising his discipline. He did not shrink from that danger any more than he feared the royal lions or the royal fires. Let them light lamps every day, then, lamps that give no light; let them fasten laurels to doorposts that will soon wither, doorposts destined for fire. These things are fitting for them — both the testimonies of darkness and the omens of punishment. You are the light of the world, and an evergreen tree (Matt 5:14). If you have renounced temples, do not make your doorway a temple. I have said too little: if you have renounced brothels, do not bring the face of a new brothel into your own home.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text, including the nuances of the theological arguments regarding the demonic nature of certain domestic rites. All scripture citations (Matt 22:21, Dan 3:18, Matt 5:14) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant clauses. The distinction between 'offices' (officia) and 'persons' (personas) is preserved. The translation of the Roman deities (Cardea, Forculus, Limentinus, Janus) is faithful to the source.
